**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget scheduled enrichment before stopping Fly**

For scheduled production runs, `.github/workflows/artist-enrichment-daily.yml:33` still sets `TDF_API_BASE` to `https://tdf-hq.fly.dev` and lines 67–78 execute enrichment in production mode. With both Fly API machines stopped and their TDF role set to `NOLOGIN` as recorded here, every daily run targets the retired backend rather than the current Hetzner database and cannot perform enrichment. Retarget or pause this workflow before treating the old writers as retired.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Follow-up 7def35976f62dd153127d25217e22d3f0d19f3aa: Retargeted the scheduled/manual artist enrichment API base to https://api.tdfrecords.net. Existing scope, publication policy, authentication and concurrency are unchanged. All messaging/enrichment regressions (111 tests) and CI contract tests (25) passed. No production enrichment run or deployment was manually triggered.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Complete the authentication and upload gates before declaring success**

In this deployed state, writes have already been enabled even though these end-to-end checks remain unperformed, while the cutover procedure in `ops/hetzner/README.md:143-145` explicitly requires Google authentication and uploads to be verified before reopening writes. This leaves two user-facing write paths unvalidated after the hostname, database, and asset-storage migration despite the record calling the cutover complete; either perform those gates or record an explicit waiver and keep the cutover status incomplete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Follow-up 7def35976f62dd153127d25217e22d3f0d19f3aa: Corrected both documents to label cutover validation incomplete and distinguish the observed traffic/writer transition from the unperformed Google interactive-login and authenticated-upload gates. No gate waiver is claimed. This thread remains open until an authorized operator performs and records those end-to-end checks; the audit has not deployed or performed production writes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget messaging-token refreshes to Hetzner**

In the stopped-Fly state recorded here, the hourly `.github/workflows/check-messaging-token.yml:56-65` still runs mutating maintenance with `FLY_APP_NAME=tdf-hq`, and `scripts/check-messaging-token.mjs:175-188` persists refreshed Instagram/Facebook tokens only through `flyctl secrets set`. When either credential enters its refresh window, the live Hetzner `api.env` will not receive the replacement, so messaging will eventually use an expired credential while the retired Fly app is mutated instead; move rotation to the current deployment's secret store or make this schedule read-only.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Follow-up 7def35976f62dd153127d25217e22d3f0d19f3aa: The hourly and manual workflow now invokes the existing read-only --check path, rejects refresh requests, and contains no Fly setup or credentials. Missing, invalid, expired and soon-expiring tokens still fail and notify. Existing exhaustive validity/expiry tests and workflow guard tests pass. A reviewed Hetzner secret-store integration remains pending; the runbook explicitly requires operator rotation and synchronization of GitHub check credentials and does not mistake those for live-service verification. No credentials were changed.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Point the course publisher at the live API**

After this cutover, the documented production command in `docs/courses/README.md:19-28` still leaves the API base unset and identifies the Fly hostname as live, while `scripts/upsert-course.mjs:8-12` therefore posts to `https://tdf-hq.fly.dev`. With the old machines stopped and their database role disabled, operators following that runbook cannot publish courses to the live Hetzner database; update both the helper default and its production instructions to use `https://api.tdfrecords.net`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Follow-up 7def35976f62dd153127d25217e22d3f0d19f3aa: Updated the course publisher default and production documentation to https://api.tdfrecords.net. Three mocked-request checks passed: production default, explicit course-base override precedence, and legacy VITE base override. Bearer authentication and request payload are unchanged; no course was published.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget the manual artist-enrichment entry point**

Although this retargets the scheduled job, the fresh missed path beyond the prior scheduled-run issue is the documented manual workflow: `scripts/artist-enrichment.mjs:19` still defaults to `https://tdf-hq.fly.dev`, and every command in `docs/artist-enrichment-runbook.md:80-121` relies on that default. After the old machines and database role are disabled, operators running dry-runs, bounded production runs, or media ingestion from the runbook will contact the retired backend unless they know to add an undocumented override; update the script default and runbook alongside this workflow.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 5486b49144f9b0d5576cef5f2e59d927c66e334f. Manual enrichment now defaults to https://api.tdfrecords.net and retains explicit TDF_API_BASE/API_BASE overrides. The runbook documents these and points backup/recovery operations to the current guarded Hetzner procedure, preserving post-cutover writes. A mocked production-API boundary regression verifies all three routing cases without network writes. All 113 messaging/enrichment tests and the exact specification gate (3 inventory and 9 evidence/escrow regressions) pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the messaging-token operator guide**

When an expiring token requires maintenance, the primary guide still states at `docs/INSTAGRAM_TOKEN_SETUP.md:160-164` that the hourly schedule and manual `action=refresh` perform automatic refresh and update Fly. This change instead rejects `refresh` and makes the schedule read-only, so an operator following that guide cannot rotate the credential and may incorrectly assume the hourly job still maintains it until messaging fails; replace those instructions with the new Hetzner rotation procedure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 5486b49144f9b0d5576cef5f2e59d927c66e334f. Updated the primary messaging guide: scheduled/manual checks are read-only, action=refresh is rejected, and legacy Fly maintenance is explicitly retired. The guide states automated Hetzner rotation is not implemented and gives the authorized operator sequence: validated replacement, secure current runtime persistence under existing deployment controls, live verification, then GitHub check-secret synchronization. Failures remain visible. No credential rotation, deployment or completion claim was made. All 113 messaging/enrichment tests and the exact specification gate (3 inventory and 9 evidence/escrow regressions) pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget social-webhook repair commands before stopping Fly**

Once the old Fly API is stopped as recorded here, the active diagnostic at `scripts/diagnose-social.mjs:53-60` still tells operators to repair missing Instagram and Facebook subscriptions by registering callbacks under `tdf-hq.fly.dev`. In the exact scenario where either subscription must be recreated, following the generated command routes inbound messages to the stopped backend; change those callback URLs to `api.tdfrecords.net` as part of the cutover.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 5486b49144f9b0d5576cef5f2e59d927c66e334f. Both missing-subscription repair commands now target the canonical API callbacks. They print environment placeholders instead of supplied secret values; the refresh guidance uses the current secret-store procedure and no longer recommends Fly updates/restarts. The mocked diagnostic regression verifies both URLs and absence of supplied credentials/retired repair commands. No provider subscription was changed. All 113 messaging/enrichment tests and the exact specification gate (3 inventory and 9 evidence/escrow regressions) pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Detect stale webhook callbacks before suppressing repairs**

When Meta returns an existing `instagram` or `page` subscription whose `callback_url` still targets `tdf-hq.fly.dev` (or whose `active` flag is false), the object remains truthy, so these new Hetzner repair commands are never shown and the summary reports no subscription issue. In that post-cutover state inbound messages continue going to the stopped backend; compare the returned callback and active state with the expected `api.tdfrecords.net` endpoint and offer repair whenever either is wrong.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in e762f67b2720b3337c8409b6c3b652224f090083. The diagnostic now requires active=true and the exact current callback URL for each subscription. Missing, inactive or stale callbacks trigger the corresponding repair command and summary issue. Regression cases exercise both channels with stale URLs, inactive current URLs and active current URLs, without provider calls. All 115 messaging/enrichment regressions and the unchanged specification inventory check pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the configured token in the Facebook repair command**

When the Facebook subscription is missing, copying this generated command submits the literal `YOUR_FACEBOOK_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN`, even though no such environment variable or separate backend setting exists. The Facebook verifier in `tdf-hq/src/TDF/ServerExtra.hs` accepts the configured Facebook messaging token, with `INSTAGRAM_VERIFY_TOKEN` as fallback, so Meta's callback challenge will be rejected unless the operator notices and manually substitutes the placeholder; emit one of the configured accepted values as the Instagram command already does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in e762f67b2720b3337c8409b6c3b652224f090083. The Facebook repair command now expands the configured FACEBOOK_MESSAGING_TOKEN, its supported FACEBOOK_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN alias, or INSTAGRAM_VERIFY_TOKEN fallback. These match the existing Config/ServerExtra verification contract. The command prints environment references rather than secret values. A local curl-stub regression executes all three expansions and verifies the accepted token is supplied without network writes. All 115 messaging/enrichment regressions and the unchanged specification inventory check pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget the bundled artist importer**

With both old API machines stopped, running the active, tested importer without an explicit override still sends its mutating party POSTs to Fly because `tdf-hq/scripts/create_artists_from_list.sh:17` defaults `BASE_URL` to `https://tdf-hq.fly.dev`. Operators following the documented bundled-import flow will therefore fail against the retired backend rather than create parties in the live Hetzner database; retarget this default alongside the other manual artist tools.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 36aff567c1d6daeb63088a765dc5e48e69fe2d09. The bundled importer now defaults to https://api.tdfrecords.net while preserving BASE_URL overrides, reviewed entity types and stable idempotency keys. The curl-stub regression verifies all 31 default requests, override routing, retry identity and fail-fast behavior. The login-helper production example is also corrected. No parties were created. All 121 helper/token/enrichment/import tests, 34 CI/evidence regressions, three inventory tests and the current inventory check pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget payment webhook runbooks**

When a Stripe or PayPal callback must be recreated, the production instructions still direct operators to the stopped backend: `SERVICE_STOREFRONT_DEPLOYMENT.md:49-50`, `STRIPE_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md:30`, `STRIPE_TICKETING_CHECKLIST.md:21`, and `scripts/test-stripe-integration.sh:98` all prescribe `tdf-hq.fly.dev`. Following any of these after the recorded callback migration would route payment events away from the live API, so update the active payment runbooks and helper output to the canonical Hetzner endpoints.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 36aff567c1d6daeb63088a765dc5e48e69fe2d09. Updated all identified active payment callback URLs and helper output to the canonical API. The guides point to the current guarded runtime procedure and preserve webhook IDs/signing secrets and existing provider/environment gates; obsolete deployment instructions are removed or explicitly marked historical. The helper no longer claims unperformed payment tests passed and fails on an unhealthy/unreachable health probe, covered by a mocked regression in the existing repo-quality suite. No payment, webhook or deployment was performed. All 121 helper/token/enrichment/import tests, 34 CI/evidence regressions, three inventory tests and the current inventory check pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor aliases in the Instagram repair command**

When the diagnostic is run with the aliases it explicitly accepts (`META_APP_ID`/`META_APP_SECRET`), or with the backend-supported `IG_VERIFY_TOKEN`, it can detect a stale subscription but the printed command expands only `FACEBOOK_APP_ID`, `FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET`, and `INSTAGRAM_VERIFY_TOKEN`. Copying that command therefore submits an empty app path, access token, or verify token even though the diagnostic itself had valid credentials; use shell fallbacks for the accepted aliases without interpolating their secret values.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 36aff567c1d6daeb63088a765dc5e48e69fe2d09. Both printed callback commands now retain FACEBOOK/META app credential fallbacks and INSTAGRAM_VERIFY_TOKEN/IG_VERIFY_TOKEN fallback without interpolating secret values. A local curl-stub regression verifies canonical and alias-only configurations expand the correct app URL, access token and verifier. Existing Facebook primary/alias/fallback and redaction tests still pass. All 121 helper/token/enrichment/import tests, 34 CI/evidence regressions, three inventory tests and the current inventory check pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize the Hetzner asset host as managed**

When enrichment now runs against the new production API, artist hero images served from `https://api.tdfrecords.net/assets/serve/...` are still rejected by `isTdfManagedImageUrl`, whose allowlist only includes the retired Fly host and `.tdfrecords.com`. Production and audit runs consequently call `persistHotlinkReview`, persist a false `link_validation_broken` source, and report `existing_third_party_hotlink_requires_authorized_ingestion` for first-party assets; add the canonical `.net` API host to the managed-image check and cover it in the retargeting test.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 7f1d2d74877c5e603097e44cc643834e1932a69e. Added only the exact canonical api.tdfrecords.net host to managed-image recognition, retaining existing managed/legacy hosts. Canonical assets no longer receive third-party hotlink reviews solely because of the cutover. Regressions accept the canonical asset and existing legacy/Drive hosts while rejecting lookalike hosts, unrelated third-party hosts and malformed URLs. All 122 helper/token/enrichment/import tests and the current specification inventory check pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget the production catalog inventory**

With both old API machines stopped and the TDF Fly role disabled, the documented production inventory command can no longer inspect production: `scripts/production-catalog-inventory.mjs:192-213` still fetches Fly health/version, lists Fly machines, and shells into the retained Fly database. It will either fail on the stopped API or, if the app is restarted, inventory the stale pre-cutover TDF database rather than Hetzner, so catalog governance reports can no longer be refreshed accurately; retarget this helper to the current deployment or explicitly retire it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 102662f13e690394ba87267e34dc513a5496ed40. Replaced retired Fly discovery/SQL transport with the existing dedicated Hetzner SSH connection, verified from the deployment record and live host. Require strict SSH host identity, running production project/service/directory, API-to-database network/name binding and configured immutable image. Compare public health/commit with the inspected API and deployment identity before/after the unchanged bounded anonymized SQL. PostgreSQL starts read-only; original transaction/timeouts/exclusions remain. Live verified inventory succeeded: 766 records, 623 tables, database tdf_hq, read-only on, API commit cc244b1f86603055997b51379b297baebfd3e7ce. Private data/credential values are not in the audit report. Six access regressions, six mail regressions, three catalog regressions and the current specification/evidence gates pass. Tests reject stale/incorrect bindings, changed deployments, unsafe credential permissions and secret-output failures.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Move mail monitoring off the stopped Fly API**

After this cutover, the installed daily mail-deliverability monitor cannot read the mailbox credentials: `scripts/mail-deliverability-monitor.py:125-140` requires a healthy `tdf-hq` Fly API machine and obtains `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD` through `flyctl ssh`, while the runbook says both machines are stopped. Every scheduled run will therefore record `mailbox_read_failed` and skip bounce/DMARC mailbox collection; update the monitor and its installed copy to use an authorized Hetzner secret source.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 102662f13e690394ba87267e34dc513a5496ed40. Moved credential retrieval to the existing protected Hetzner api.env, requiring mode-0600 protection, the verified production container/image/database identity, and agreement with runtime SMTP configuration. Only the two needed keys cross SSH into process memory; stderr/exception values are redacted. Read-only IMAP, BODY.PEEK, size limits, aggregate-only reports and failure behavior remain. Rechecked and atomically updated the installed monitor/helper with verified hashes; the existing LaunchAgent was unchanged and its exact scheduled command passed live with mailboxReadSucceeded=true, eight aggregate reports and zero errors. No email was sent. Six access regressions, six mail regressions, three catalog regressions and the current specification/evidence gates pass. Tests reject stale/incorrect bindings, changed deployments, unsafe credential permissions and secret-output failures.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget the primary platform deployment guide**

After this move, the repository's primary `DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` still identifies Fly as production and, at lines 317–337, instructs operators to configure Cloudflare Pages with `VITE_API_BASE=https://tdf-hq.fly.dev`. The next frontend deployment performed from that guide would rebuild the production UI against the stopped backend instead of the live Hetzner API; update the guide to use `https://api.tdfrecords.net` or clearly retire it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 4031ed4a2c8f6c84df5e2a03b920f2643c16bd18. Retired DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md as a production procedure with an explicit top-level notice and links to the current Hetzner runbook and outstanding validation. Historical provider/secret/migration/rollback commands are explicitly non-operative, and retained Trader/shared Fly resources are protected. Both Cloudflare and Vercel frontend examples now use the canonical API. Regenerated the single guide fingerprint; inventory validation, three Python and nine Node gate regressions pass. All 122 helper/token/enrichment/import tests and the current specification inventory check pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire the standalone Fly token refresher**

When an operator uses the repository's standalone refresh helper during the manual rotation described here, `scripts/refresh-messaging-token.mjs:124-138` still prints Fly secret/restart commands and `--auto` executes them against `tdf-hq`, leaving the live Hetzner credentials unchanged. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier workflow finding is that this separate executable remains active even though this section says not to update the retired Fly application; retire its auto mode or make it persist through the current secret-management procedure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 4d40ae58c07a0be8c4394aecfbda2249b0a1c462. Retired the standalone refresher in both normal and --auto modes: it fails before token exchange, credential output, secret writes or service restarts, and points to the current protected-secret runbook. Regression subprocesses exercise both modes with sentinel credentials and verify nonzero exit, empty stdout, no credential disclosure and no Fly commands. The existing health monitor is retained; no credential rotation was performed. Both retired-helper regressions, three specification regressions and nine evidence/escrow cases pass. Earlier live catalog/mail checks remain unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire the remaining payment deployment guides**

When payment configuration is next changed, active repository guides still direct it to the stopped backend despite this recorded callback migration. A fresh repo-wide search after the prior payment-runbook fix finds `STRIPE_TICKETING_DEPLOYMENT_SUMMARY.md:34-80` instructing operators to register the Fly webhook, write Fly secrets, and rebuild the frontend with the Fly API, while `VERIFICATION.md:14-53` likewise manages PayPal secrets and health on Fly; following either procedure would update or route traffic to the retired service, so these guides also need current Hetzner instructions or an explicit historical-retirement notice.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 4d40ae58c07a0be8c4394aecfbda2249b0a1c462. Added explicit top-level historical-retirement notices to STRIPE_TICKETING_DEPLOYMENT_SUMMARY.md and VERIFICATION.md, identifying the current canonical API/runbook and declaring the old Fly webhook/secret/restart/frontend commands non-operative. The notices preserve provider identity/signature, release gates and the retained Trader/shared database. Generated document fingerprints are current; specification and evidence gates pass. Both retired-helper regressions, three specification regressions and nine evidence/escrow cases pass. Earlier live catalog/mail checks remain unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare the configured digest with the image reference**

On the actual digest-pinned Compose deployment, the top-level `Image` returned by `docker inspect` is the local image/config ID, while `TDF_IMAGE` contains the registry manifest reference (`name@sha256:...`); these hashes differ even when the container was created from the correct image. This check therefore rejects a healthy deployment before either the catalog query or `mail_credentials()` can run, breaking both newly retargeted tools. Compare against `Config.Image` or a matching `RepoDigest`; the test currently masks this by assigning the same synthetic `sha256:abc` value to both fields.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in f528eee8c74d78444c2cda05160cb101e737d4de. Compare the configured immutable registry reference with Config.Image or a matching image RepoDigest. Retain the local image/config ID only for race detection. Tests now deliberately use different local/config and manifest hashes, accept the matching reference/RepoDigest, and reject a wrong registry digest. Live current-host catalog and installed mail checks pass with the corrected verification. Eight access, six mail, three catalog, three retired-helper, three specification and nine evidence/escrow cases pass. Final live catalog and installed mailbox checks pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire the remaining Instagram diagnostic's Fly commands**

When the read-only check reports an unhealthy Instagram token and an operator uses the root-level diagnostic, `scripts/diagnose-instagram.mjs:18-25` and `:144-146` still instruct them to write the credential to `tdf-hq` and restart that retired Fly app. Following those instructions leaves the live Hetzner credential unchanged. Fresh evidence beyond the existing standalone-refresher finding is that this separate executable remains active and is not labeled historical; retarget or retire its repair output alongside this new rotation procedure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in f528eee8c74d78444c2cda05160cb101e737d4de. Retired the separate legacy Instagram diagnostic before it can display token prefixes or call providers. It now fails with a pointer to the existing read-only check-messaging-token.mjs and current protected-secret runbook. A subprocess regression supplies sentinel credentials and verifies no token prefix, Fly command, provider request or restart path is exposed. Eight access, six mail, three catalog, three retired-helper, three specification and nine evidence/escrow cases pass. Final live catalog and installed mailbox checks pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce read-only access with database privileges**

When `production_access.py inventory` receives SQL containing `SET default_transaction_read_only=off` or an explicit read-write transaction, this session default can be overridden because `psql` connects as the `postgres` superuser. Since the CLI forwards arbitrary stdin, an erroneous or repurposed invocation can mutate the live production database despite the helper's read-only contract; execute through a genuinely read-only database role rather than relying solely on `PGOPTIONS`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in f528eee8c74d78444c2cda05160cb101e737d4de. Catalog queries now connect as tdf_catalog_inventory, not postgres, and arbitrary stdin is rejected unless it matches the reviewed inventory SQL digest. Provisioned the dedicated SELECT-only/no-password role using the existing authorized operator connection: 623 readable tables, zero writable tables, no schema CREATE, superuser, role/database creation or row-security bypass. The first setup correctly rolled back on inherited PUBLIC schema CREATE; the corrected setup explicitly preserves all existing named roles effective CREATE capabilities before removing the ambient grant. Existing login/membership and application data are unchanged. Verified an actual zero-row UPDATE is permission-denied even after SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE and disabling the session default; live full catalog inventory succeeds. New-table access gaps fail closed. Eight access, six mail, three catalog, three retired-helper, three specification and nine evidence/escrow cases pass. Final live catalog and installed mailbox checks pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retire the remaining Instagram token helper**

A separate active entry point remains outside this retirement: `scripts/get-instagram-token.mjs:46-49,85-99` reads and displays a stored token prefix, then instructs operators to write `INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN` to `tdf-hq` and restart Fly. When used for the next Instagram credential rotation, it exposes part of the credential and updates the stopped backend instead of the protected Hetzner configuration; retire or retarget this helper alongside the two scripts covered here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 9a8357065fb45d4565e1bd4a764d5f9fe739a40d. Retired the separate get-instagram-token helper before it reads stored state or prints token prefixes. It now fails with the existing OAuth/current protected-configuration and read-only health-check paths. A subprocess regression places a sentinel stored token in an isolated working directory and verifies empty stdout, no prefix disclosure and no Fly repair command. Four retired-helper regressions, three inventory and nine evidence/escrow tests pass. Existing live catalog/mail validation remains unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retarget the payment audit callback table**

Although this records that both provider callbacks were migrated, the current `PAYMENT_AUDIT.md:249-254` still labels the Fly URLs as the webhook endpoints to configure. If either Stripe or PayPal callback is recreated from that audit, events will be routed to the stopped backend rather than the live API; update those endpoints to `api.tdfrecords.net` or explicitly retire the audit as an operational reference.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 9a8357065fb45d4565e1bd4a764d5f9fe739a40d. Corrected both active PAYMENT_AUDIT callback-table origins to https://api.tdfrecords.net while preserving their exact existing paths and event sets. Added a guard to preserve account/webhook identities and signature verification and to use the current release procedure; no provider configuration was changed. Regenerated the audit-document fingerprint and passed the specification/evidence gates. Four retired-helper regressions, three inventory and nine evidence/escrow tests pass. Existing live catalog/mail validation remains unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the public API check to the inspected deployment**

The public and SSH-side APIs are correlated only by their Git commit and generic health payloads. If `api.tdfrecords.net` is accidentally routed back to Fly—or to any other healthy deployment running the same SHA—this check still passes because `provider`, `project`, and container identity all come from the SSH-side metadata rather than the public response. That defeats the stated fail-closed origin check and can produce an inventory report that combines public status from one deployment with data from Hetzner; compare a deployment-unique identity exposed through both paths (or otherwise verify the public origin) before running the query.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 82c4c448a77ca88d53dc634f1f392d57c84b17b2. Bound both public health/version requests to the server address reported by the authenticated SSH connection: every public DNS answer and the actual HTTPS socket peer must match, while normal TLS certificate/hostname verification remains enabled and redirects are rejected.
